title: Sum comes back NaN
explanation: With <=, the last iteration reads nums[3], which is undefined, and 6 + undefined is NaN. Valid indexes stop at length - 1.
hint: What are the valid indexes of a 3-element array?

title: An even number survives
explanation: splice shifts every later element one place left, then i++ skips the element that just moved into slot i. Build a new array with filter, or loop backwards if you must mutate.
hint: After splice removes index i, which element is now at index i?

title: Empty average isn't 0
explanation: NaN is the only value that isn't equal to itself, so avg === NaN is always false. Use Number.isNaN, or check nums.length === 0 before dividing.

title: Points come back undefined
explanation: After =>, a { starts a function body, not an object. The body evaluates x, y and returns nothing. Wrap an object literal in parentheses to return it.
hint: After an arrow, how does JavaScript read a {?

title: Posts never arrive
explanation: Each .then passes on whatever its callback returns. This callback has braces and no return, so the next step gets undefined right away, without waiting for the posts.
hint: What does the first .then callback return?

title: Christmas lands in January
explanation: Date months run from 0 (January) to 11 (December). Month 12 rolls over to January of the next year. Days, oddly, start at 1.
hint: What number does new Date() use for January?

title: Only the first space is replaced
explanation: With a string pattern, replace only changes the first match. Use replaceAll, or a regex with the g flag: .replace(/\s+/g, '-').
hint: How many matches does replace change when the pattern is a plain string?

title: Reversed list has one node
explanation: Line 4 overwrites cur.next before it's saved, so line 6 moves to prev (null on the first pass) instead of the rest of the list. Save next first.
hint: By the time line 6 reads cur.next, what's in it?

title: Sort order is unreliable
prompt: Should put the oldest person first. For some inputs, the order comes back wrong.
explanation: A comparator must return a negative, zero or positive number. A boolean becomes 1 or 0, so it can never say "a goes first", and the result depends on the engine's sorting algorithm.
hint: What kind of value does sort expect its compare function to return?

title: The listener won't go away
fix:
const onClick = () => log('click');
// pass the same onClick to add and remove
explanation: removeEventListener only removes the exact same function object. Each arrow expression creates a new function, so nothing matches. Keep a reference to the handler, or use an AbortController signal.
hint: Are two identical-looking arrow functions the same function?
